items.headline: Nvidia weighs $10bn anchor stake in Anthropic's IPO — buying its own demand
items.note: Nvidia is reportedly negotiating a second $10bn commitment to Anthropic, this time as an IPO anchor investor on top of its November 2025 compute-linked $10bn stake, at a targeted $2tn valuation and up to $100bn raise. Financial press (Motley Fool, Yahoo, PYMNTS) is unanimous in framing this as Nvidia funding its own chip demand — a live, breaking instantiation of the published essay's circular-financing thesis, useful for a distribution follow-up or native post rather than a new essay.

items.headline: AI is hollowing out entry-level roles, UK employer survey finds
items.source: CNBC (syndicated copy; original CNBC 23 Sep behind a paywall block)
items.note: Open University/mid-market survey: 51% of UK business leaders say AI is changing hiring, 19% have cut entry-level recruitment (42% of those citing AI). London ad agency Catalyst has one junior now covering five accounts AI used to need several staff for. Directly instantiates the holding-pen title with fresh named-source quotes, but survey-level figures rather than a dollar amount cap the number score.

items.headline: AI token prices keep falling — Morgan Stanley flags $300bn of data-centre bonds as exposed
items.note: Ramp spending data shows effective token prices down ~41% from March's peak; OpenAI's effective price down 38% since 1 August to 48 cents, Anthropic's down 22% to 90 cents. Morgan Stanley says up to $300bn of bonds financing data-centre builds are vulnerable if prices don't stabilise. Strong dollar figure and named bank source, but the trend is a few weeks old rather than a fresh 24-hour break, so velocity is marked down.

items.headline: Alphabet's cloud surge outruns Meta's AI capex bet, capex-ROI scorecard shows
items.note: Google Cloud revenue up 82% to $24.77bn against $44.92bn of Q2 capex, versus Meta's Q2 capex of $30.12bn and an operating-margin collapse to 31% from 43%. Pre-empts the 'depreciation cliff' trigger (hyperscaler earnings, late October) with hard comparative figures, but it's a single trade-press recap of already-reported Q2 numbers rather than a fresh earnings print, so it doesn't clear the bar to propose a new working title.

items.headline: Buyback announcements on pace for a 10-year quarterly low as dividend cuts spike
items.note: Only 91 buyback authorisations in Q3 2026 (as of 14 September), on track for the lowest quarterly count in the dataset's 10-year history; 19% of announcements are dividend reductions, the highest share since Q2 2020. On-theme for the Buffett/capital-allocation family and precise, countable figures, but a niche trade outlet and a two-week-old snapshot keep magnitude and velocity low.
